_comment: Mutants that put the BUILD CONTEXT hole BACK into the branch.
FINDING (review panel run #6, 2026-11-11, hermes, counted YES):
`pwa/` is its own docker build context (`context: ./pwa` in
docker-compose.yml) and `pwa/Dockerfile.prod` does `COPY . .`, but
`pwa/` had NO .dockerignore, while `frontend/` HAS one. A build context
uses the .dockerignore in ITS OWN ROOT, so the root .dockerignore does
not apply to the pwa image at all: a gitignored file inside pwa/ was
copied into that image, and `git status --porcelain` does not report
ignored files -- so the deploy stamp could not see it and the published
archive did not contain it. The offer promises the archive of the
stamped commit IS the exact tree of the running build.
MEASURED on production before the fix (2026-11-11): pwa/.dockerignore
does not exist on the host and pwa/ currently holds no gitignored file,
so the hole was LATENT, not live. The fix closes it.
SECOND HOLE, THE SAME CLASS (2026-11-11, claude's residual on panel
run #7, confirmed in code): git consults the NEAREST .gitignore, so a
file ignored by the CONTEXT'S OWN .gitignore is invisible to
`git status --porcelain` as well -- and the rule set of a context did
not cover the context's own .gitignore at all. `frontend/.gitignore`
ignores `*.local`, `dist-ssr`, `.DS_Store`, `*.suo`, `*.ntvs*`,
`*.njsproj`, `*.sln`, `*.sw?` and `alembic/versions/*`, and NONE of
those were covered: such a file was copied into the image while the
deploy stamp could not see it. Both contexts now carry those rules,
and the guard asks the forward rule against BOTH .gitignore files.
MEASURED: adding them excludes ZERO tracked files (the reverse rule
stays exact), so the fix cannot sweep committed code out of an image.
These mutants remove ONE rule from ONE context's rule set, and the
guard must catch every one of them:
* removing a DEPTH form leaves the nested copy uncovered (the rule is
'excluded at the context root, at depth 1 and at depth 2');
* removing the re-inclusion of the tracked .env.production sweeps a
TRACKED file out of the context, which the reverse rule catches.
Every needle below occurs EXACTLY ONCE in its target file (asserted by
tests/test_deployed_commit_mutation_needles.py and re-checked by the
harness).
Run with:  python tools/mutation_harness.py tools/mutations/build_context_dockerignore.json
NEVER run concurrently with a test run or a reviewer.

mutations.label: M1: the DEPTH form of the underscore-separated env-copy class is gone from the pwa context, so a NESTED .env_backup enters the pwa image
M2: the DEPTH form of node_modules is gone from the pwa context, so a NESTED node_modules enters the pwa image and overwrites the one the image installed
M3: the pwa context no longer re-includes the tracked .env.production, so the image would be built without the env file the build reads and the published archive would not match the image
M4: the DEPTH form of node_modules is gone from the frontend context, so a NESTED node_modules enters the frontend image and overwrites the one the image installed

M5: the DEPTH form of the '*.local' class is gone from the frontend context, so a NESTED x.local enters the frontend image -- and it is ignored by frontend/.gitignore, so `git status --porcelain` cannot report it
M6: the DEPTH form of the 'dist-ssr' class is gone from the pwa context, so a NESTED dist-ssr enters the pwa image -- and it is ignored by pwa/.gitignore, so `git status --porcelain` cannot report it

M7: the rule that covers frontend/.gitignore inside the ROOT context is gone, so a NESTED frontend/sub/x.local enters the SIX images that build from the root context (api, bot, celery_worker, market_data, mcp-memory, websocket) while `git status --porcelain` cannot report it
